name: November 19, 2024 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  NOVEMBER 19, 2024
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Commissioner Skophammer called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dane Skophammer, Vice Chair Alicia Peak (arrived at 6:32 p.m.),
  Commissioners Georgia Goldfarb (arrived at 7:04 p.m.), Suzanne Guldimann, and Jake
  Lingo

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Kate Manisco,
  Recreation Manager; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Skophammer led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  Vice Chair Peak arrived at 6:32 p.m.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Chair Skophammer seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4—0;
  Commissioner Goldfarb absent (arrived at 7:04 p.m.).

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on November l4, 2024.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Joe Sichta proposed that Class Aquatics share pool time with the Malibu Marlins
  at the Malibu Community Pool. He stated that multiple swimmers from the Malibu
  Aquatics Foundation had joined Class Aquatics. He stated that Class Aquatics

  would bring their program to Malibu so that swimmers could have a competitive
  local swim team and families would not have to travel outside of Malibu. He also
  requested the Commission to investigate the three swimmers per lane rule. He
  stated no other swimming organizations had that rule.

  Vice Chair Peak stated pool space between multiple organizations was proposed
  before the Request for Qualifications was released, and Malibu Aquatics
  Foundation opposed having multiple organizations simultaneously on the swim
  deck.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Peak moved, and Commissioner Guldimann seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4—0;
  Commissioner Goldfarb was absent (arrived at 7:04 p.m.).

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previouslv Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  l.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the October 15, 2024
  Parks and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Communitv Services Department Monthlv Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in October 2024.

  Commissioner Goldfarb arrived at 7:04 p.m.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  Malibu Equestrian Park Update
  Recommended Action: 1) Receive and flle a report on Malibu Equestrian Park
  attendance from July 8 to November 12, 2024; and 2) Provide feedback to staff
  regarding program recommendations.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Recreation Manager Manisco provided historical information on the Malibu
  Equestrian Park.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo confirmed
  the City does not pay a school district fee; however, the City maintains and pays all
  fees related to maintenance and upkeep.

  Commissioner Lingo inquired if the property or an arena could be converted into a
  different amenity since the park was underutilized.

  Commissioner Guldimann opposed park changes and stated that the park's
  equestrian heritage should be preserved.

  Commissioner Lingo stated he was sensitive to the equestrian community and
  wanted to explore park options to serve the community in other ways.

  Commissioner Guldimann suggested planning park activities that would not require
  staff to be present.

  Vice Chair Peak indicated agreement with Commissioner Lingo. She stated that the
  City could invest in upgrades for walkers or other activities since equestrian use
  was minimal. She suggested the addition of a BMX track around the arenas.

  Commissioner Guldimann opposed a BMX track. She stated it would not be
  compatible with equestrian users.

  In response to Commissioner Lingo, Commissioner Guldimann stated a BMX track
  would dissuade equestrian users from visiting even with designated hours.

  Chair Skophammer stated the City should wait for decisions on school separation
  before providing a recommendation on new amenities or alterations. He suggested
  staff enhance the trails and work with Trancas Riders and Ropers to coordinate
  equestrian programming.

  Vice Chair Peak suggested partnering with Malibu High School to provide
  programs.

  Commissioner Lingo stated dual purposes for the park should be considered.

  Chair Skophammer suggested reviewing use options with Trancas Riders and
  Ropers and the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District and requested staff
  to continue to collect data and monitor usage.

MOTION  Vice Chair Peak moved, and Commissioner Lingo seconded a motion to collect
  data yearly using the trail cameras from May through June and explore potential
  park use with the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District. The question was
  called, and the motion carried 3-2; Commissioners Goldfarb and Guldimann
  dissenting.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Parks and Recreation Commission Mid—Year ActivitV Report

  Recommended Action: Review and approve the Parks and Recreation Commission
  Mid—Year Activity Report covering the period from July through December 2024.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Chair Skophammer stated he wanted to reorder the activities based on importance.
  He requested Community Lands be moved to the top of the list.

  Vice Chair Peak recommended adding an item related to the Ad Hoc Committee
  reviewing and providing feedback to the Commission on the Aquatics Program
  Request for Qualifications (RFQ) process.

  Chair Skophammer requested to add the 2024 Jake Kuredjian Award presentation.
  He also recommended moving the baseball field conversion to the second item.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated she would include an item covering
  the installation of the trail cameras at the Equestrian Park and reviewing and
  providing feedback on the Trancas Canyon Park Dog Park rules.

MOTION  Chair Skophammer moved, and Vice Chair Peak seconded a motion to approve the
  Parks and Recreation Commission Mid-Year Activity report revising 1) the order
  of activities based on their importance with the Community Lands item first and
  the baseball field conversion second; 2) adding an item appointing the Ad Hoc
  Committee to review and provide feedback to the Commission on the Aquatics
  Program Request for Qualifications (RFQ) process; 3) add the presentation of the
  2024 Jake Kuredjian Award; 4) add the installation of trail cameras at the
  Equestrian Park; and 5) add reviewed and provided feedback on the Trancas
  Canyon Park Dog Park rules. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Manager Manisco provided an update on the Halloween Bu Bash,
  Senior Resource Fair, Malibu Marlins Swim Team, Afterschool Programs
  Feedback Survey, Youth Basketball League, Winter Recreation Guide, and
  Contractor Recruitment.

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on the Native Plant Walk
  and Giveaway, Charmlee Park Night Hike, Broad Fire Update, City Hall Winter
  Closure, and the December Commission meeting.

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus, the Commission would meet for its Regular Meeting on December
  l7, 2024.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Vice Chair Peak inquired if a fence could be installed at Malibu Bluffs Park to
  prevent balls and kids from entering the Broad Fire burn area.

  Commissioner Goldfarb supported offering programs with the Malibu Marlins and
  Class Aquatics.

  Commissioner Lingo requested information on the three-person per lane rule for
  the community pool.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Skophammer adjourned the meeting at 8:24 p.m.
